questions.q: A series LCR circuit consists of $R = 80 Ω$. ${X}_{L} = 100 Ω$, and ${X}_{C} = 40 Ω$. The input voltage is $2500\cos \left(100\pit\right)V$. The amplitude of current, in the circuit, is _____ $A$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Comparing input voltage with standard expression,& $V = {V}_{0}\cos \left(\omegat\right), we get~\omega =$100$\pi.

Now, impedance~$Z = $\sqrt{R^{2} + \left({X}_{L} - {X}_{C}\right)2}

=\sqrt{{80}^{2} + \left(100 - 40\right)2}

$= 100Ω$

Therefore, peak current

${i}_{0} = $\dfrac{V0}{Z} = \dfrac{2500}{100}$A = 25A$

$

questions.q: As shown in the figure an inductor of inductance $200mH$ is connected to an $AC$ source of emf $220V$and frequency~$50$ Hz. The instantaneous voltage of the source is $0V$ when the peak value of current is $\dfrac{a}{π}A$. The value of $a$& is _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The reactance of the given inductor is,

${X}_{L} = \omegaL = 2\pifL = 2\pi \times 50 \times 0 . 2 = 20\piΩ$.

The maximum current in the given circuit will be,

${i}_{0} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}{V}_{rms}}{XL} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2} \times 220}{20\pi} = \dfrac{242}{π}A$

Therefore,~$a = 242$

questions.q: A series LCR circuit is designed to resonate at an angular frequency ${ω}_{0} = {10}^{5}rads^{- 1} .$~The circuit draws $16W$ power from $120V$ source at resonance. The value of resistance $R$ in the circuit is ________~$Ω .$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
At resonance

$P = \dfrac{V2}{R}$

$R = \dfrac{V2}{P} = \dfrac{\left(120\right)2}{16}$

$= 900Ω$

questions.q: At very high frequencies, the effective impedance of the given circuit will be _________Ω .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For $\omega \to \infty$
$\dfrac{1}{\omegaC} \to 0 ⇒$ capacitance acts as short circuit
&~$\omegaL \to \infty$ Inductance acts as open circuit

$Z = 1 + \dfrac{2 \times 2}{2 + 2} = 2Ω$

questions.q: An alternating emf $\mathrm{E}=110 \sqrt{2} \sin 100 \mathrm{t}$ volt is applied to a capacitor of $2 \mu \mathrm{F}$, the rms value of current in the circuit is _____{\mathrm{mA}},
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} C & =2 \mu f ; \quad E=110 \sqrt{2} \sin (100 \mathrm{t}) \\ \mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{C}} & =\frac{1}{\omega \mathrm{c}}=\frac{1}{100 \times 2 \times 10^{-6}} \\ = & \frac{10000}{2}=5000 \Omega \\ \mathrm{i}_{\mathrm{o}} & =\frac{110 \sqrt{2}}{5000} \\ \mathrm{i}_{\mathrm{rms}} & =\frac{110 \sqrt{2}}{5000 \sqrt{2}} \\ & =\frac{110}{5} \mathrm{~mA} \\ & =22 \mathrm{~mA}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The frequencies at which the current amplitude in an LCR series circuit becomes $\dfrac{1}{2}$ times its maximum value, are $212rads^{- 1}$ and $232rads^{- 1}$. The value of resistance in the circuit is $R = 5Ω$. The self inductance in the circuit is _____~$mH$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Bandwidth of RLC circuit is& $BW = {f}_{2} - {f}_{1}= \dfrac{R}{2\piL}$

Or,~$BW = {ω}_{2} - {ω}_{1} = \dfrac{R}{L}$

$BW = 232 - 212 = \dfrac{R}{L}$

Thus, self inductance in the circuit is~$L = \dfrac{5}{20} = 250mH$

questions.q:
An inductor of inductance $2\mu H$ is connected in series with a resistance, a variable capacitor and an AC source of frequency $7kHz$. The value of capacitance for which maximum current is drawn into the circuit is~$\dfrac{1}{x}F$,~where the value of $x$ is ______.

(Take~$\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For maximum current in series LCR circuit,

${X}_{C} = {X}_{L} ⇒ \dfrac{1}{2\pifC} = 2\pifL$

$⇒ C = \dfrac{1}{4{π}^{2}f^{2}L} = \dfrac{1}{4 \times {π}^{2} \times 49 \times {10}^{6} \times 2 \times {10}^{- 6}}$

$⇒ C = \dfrac{1}{3872}F$

Therefore,~$x = 3872$.

questions.q: A capacitor of reactance $4 \sqrt{3} \Omega$ and a resistor of resistance $4 \Omega$ are connected in series with an ac source of peak value $8 \sqrt{2} \mathrm{~V}$. The power dissipation in the circuit is ________ W.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{Z}=\sqrt{\mathrm{R}^2+\mathrm{X}^2 \mathrm{~L}} \\ & \mathrm{Z}=\sqrt{4^2+(4 \sqrt{3})^2}=8 \Omega \\ & \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{rms}}=\frac{\mathrm{V}}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{8 \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}}=(8 \mathrm{~V}) \\ & \mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{rms}}=\frac{\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{rms}}}{\mathrm{Z}}=\frac{8}{8}=1 \mathrm{~A}\end{aligned}$ Power dissipated $=$\mathrm{I}$_{\mathrm{rms}}^2 \times \mathrm{R}=1 \times 4=(4 \mathrm{~W})$

questions.q: An inductor of $10mH$~is connected to a $20V$~battery through a resistor of $10kΩ$ and a switch. After a long time, when maximum current is set up in the circuit, the current is switched off. The current in the circuit after~$1\mu s$ is $\dfrac{x}{100}mA$. Then $x$ is equal to ______ . (Take $e^{- 1} = 0 . 37$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${I}_\max = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{20V}{10KΩ} = 2mA$

For $LR$-decay circuit,~

$I = {I}_\maxe^{- Rt / L}$

$I = 2mAe\dfrac{- 10 \times {10}^{3} \times 1 \times {10}^{- 6}}{10 \times {10}^{- 3}}$

$I = 2mAe^{- 1}$

$I = 2 \times 0 . 37mA$

$I = \dfrac{74}{100}mA$

$x = 74$

questions.q: An LCR series circuit of capacitance $62 . 5nF$ and resistance of $50Ω$,~is connected to an A.C. source of frequency $2 . 0kHz$. For maximum value of amplitude of current in circuit, the value of inductance is ____mH$.  \left( \text{Take}{π}^{2} = 10\right)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here,& $f = 2kHz = 2000Hz, C = 62 . 5nF = 62 . 5 \times {10}^{- 9}F\text{and}R = 50Ω$

Resonance~frequency (amplitude of the current will be maximum in this case) is given by~$f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}$, here,~$L$~is the inductance.

Putting the values,~

$2000Hz = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{L \times 62 . 5 \times {10}^{- 9}}}$

$L = \dfrac{1}{4{π}^{2} \times {2000}^{2} \times 62 . 5 \times {10}^{- 9}} = 0 . 1H = 100mH$

questions.q: To light, a $50W, 100V$ lamp is connected, in series with a capacitor of capacitance $\dfrac{50}{\pi\sqrt{x}}\muF$, with $200V, 50HzAC$ source. The value of $x$ will be _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Electrical power is given by& $P = \dfrac{V2}{R} ⇒ R = \dfrac{V2}{P}$

Resistance of lamp is~$R = \dfrac{100 \times 100}{50} ⇒ R = 200Ω$

Let~${V}_{C}$~and~${V}_{R}$~be the voltage across capacitor and resistor.

Here,~${V}_R^{2} + {V}_C^{2} = V^{2}$

Current through lamp is~$i = \dfrac{100}{200} = \dfrac{1}{2}A$

$⇒ \left(100\right)2 + {V}_C^{2} = \left(200\right)2$

$⇒ {V}_C^{2} = 30000 ⇒ {V}_{C} = 100\sqrt{3}V$

We know that,~$V = i \times {X}_{C}$

Then, ${X}_{C} = 200\sqrt{3}Ω = \dfrac{1}{ωC}$

So, capacitance of capacitor is~$C = \dfrac{1}{20 \times 50 \times 20\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{50 \times {10}^{- 6}}{x}$

$\sqrt{x} = 50 \times {10}^{- 6} \times 100 \times 200\sqrt{3}$

Thus, value of~$x = 3$.

questions.q: When a $d c$ voltage of $100 \mathrm{~V}$ is applied to an inductor, a $d c$ current of $5 \mathrm{~A}$ flows through it. When an ac voltage of $200 \mathrm{~V}$ peak value is connected to inductor, its inductive reactance is found to be $20 \sqrt{3} \Omega$. The power dissipated in the circuit is _______ W.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For DC voltage
$\mathrm{R}=\frac{\mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{I}}=\frac{100}{5}=20 \Omega$
for AC voltage
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}=20 \sqrt{3} \Omega \\
& \mathrm{R}=20 \Omega \\
& \mathrm{Z}=\sqrt{\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}^2+\mathrm{R}^2}=\sqrt{3 \times 400+400}=40 \Omega \\
& \text { Power }=\mathrm{i}_{\text {rms }}^2 \mathrm{R} \\
& \quad=\left(\frac{\mathrm{V}_{\text {rms }}}{\mathrm{Z}}\right)^2 \times \mathrm{R}=\left(\frac{\frac{200}{\sqrt{2}}}{40}\right)^2 \times 20=250 \mathrm{~W}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A transmitting station releases waves of wavelength $960m$. A capacitor of $2 . 56\muF$ is used in the resonant circuit. The self-inductance of coil necessary for resonance is $x \times {10}^{- 8}H$. find~$x$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\lambda = 960m$

$C = 2 . 56\muF = 2 . 56 \times {10}^{- 6}F$

$c = 3 \times {10}^{8}ms^{- 1}$

$L = ?$

Now at resonance, ${ω}_{0} = \dfrac{1}{LC}$~[Resonant frequency]

$2\pi{f}_{0} = \dfrac{1}{LC}$

On substituting ${f}_{0} = \dfrac{c}{λ},$~we have $2\pi\dfrac{c}{λ} = \dfrac{1}{LC}$

On substituting ${f}_{0} = \dfrac{c}{λ},$~we have $2\pi\dfrac{c}{λ} = \dfrac{1}{LC}$

Squaring both sides: $4{π}^{2}\dfrac{c2}{\lambda2} = \dfrac{1}{LC}$

$= \dfrac{4 \times 10 \times \left(3 \times {10}^{8}\right)2}{\left(960\right)2} = \dfrac{1}{L \times 2 . 56 \times {10}^{- 6}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{L} = \dfrac{4 \times 10 \times 9 \times {10}^{16} \times 2 . 56 \times {10}^{- 6}}{960 \times 960}$

$⇒ L = 10 \times {10}^{- 8}H$

questions.q: In a series LCR circuit, the inductance, capacitance and resistance are $L = 100mH$, $C = 100\muF$and $R = 10Ω$ respectively. They are connected to an $AC$ source of voltage $220V$ and frequency of $50$ Hz. The approximate value of current in the circuit will be _____~$A$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Angular frequency,& $\omega = 2\pif = 100\pi rads^{- 1}$

Here, inductive reactance ${X}_{L} = \omegaL = \left(100\pi\right)\left(100 \times {10}^{- 3}\right) = 10\piΩ$

And capacitive reactance${X}_{C} = \dfrac{1}{\omegaC} = \dfrac{1}{\left(100\pi\right) \times \left(100 \times {10}^{- 6}\right)} = \dfrac{100}{π}Ω = 10\piΩ$

Now, impedance of the series circuit is $Z = \sqrt{R^{2} + \left({X}_{L} - {X}_{C}\right)2} = R = 10Ω$

Therefore,

${I}_{RMS} = \dfrac{VRMS}{Z}$,

$= \dfrac{220}{10} = 22A$
questions.question: In a series LCR circuit, the inductance, capacitance and resistance are $L = 100mH$, $C = 100\muF$and $R = 10Ω$ respectively. They are connected to an $AC$ source of voltage $220V$ and frequency of $50$ Hz. The approximate value of current in the circuit will be _____~$A$.

questions.q: An oscillating $LC$circuit consists of a $75mH$ inductor and a $1 . 2 µ F$ capacitor. If the maximum charge to the capacitor is $2 . 7 µ C$. The maximum current in the circuit will be _______mA.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When the capacitor is fully discharged,& the current is maximum and all the energy resides in the inductor. Hence, the energy of the capacitor is equal to the energy of the inductor.

$\dfrac{Li^{2}m}{2} = \dfrac{Q^{2}m}{2C} . . . ( i )$

~where~${i}_{m}$~is the maximum current and~${Q}_{m}$~is the maximum charge.

The given values are~

${Q}_{m} = 2 . 7 \times {10}^{- 6}CL = 75 \times {10}^{- 3}HC = 1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 6}F$

The maximum current is found from equation (i)

${i}_{m} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{LC}}{Q}_{m} ⇒ {i}_{m} = \dfrac{2 . 7 \times {10}^{- 6}}{75 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 6}} = 9mA$

questions.q: For a given series LCR circuit it is found that maximum current is drawn when value of variable capacitance is $25 \mathrm{nF}$. If resistance of $200 \Omega$ and $100 \mathrm{mH}$ inductor is being used in the given circuit. The frequency of ac source is ______ $\times 10^3 \mathrm{~Hz}$. (given $\pi^2=10$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{f}_0=\frac{1}{2 \pi \sqrt{\mathrm{L} \times \mathrm{C}}} \\ & \mathrm{f}_0=\frac{1}{2 \pi \sqrt{100 \times 10^{-3} \times 25 \times 10^{-9}}} \\ & =\frac{1}{2 \pi \sqrt{25 \times 10^{-10}}} \\ & =\frac{1}{2 \pi \times 5} \times 10^5 \times \sqrt{10} \mathrm{~Hz} \\ & =\frac{100}{10} \times 10^3 \mathrm{~Hz} \\ & \mathrm{f}_0=10 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~Hz}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: An inductor of $0 . 5mH$, a capacitor of $20\mu F$ and resistance of $20Ω$ are connected in series with a $220V$ ac source. If the current is in phase with the emf, the amplitude of current of the circuit is~$\sqrt{x}A$.~The value of $x$ is-
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Here, emf and current are in phase, so the circuit is either pure resistive circuit or case of resonance,

${X}_{L} = {X}_{C}$

Thus, the impedance of circuit is $Z = \sqrt{R^{2} + \left({X}_{L} - {X}_{C}\right)2} = R = 20Ω$

Now,~rms value of current~is~${i}_{rms} = \dfrac{220}{20} = 11A$

Using the relation between peak and rms value of current, we have peak value~${i}_{0 =}{i}_{rms}\sqrt{2} = 11\sqrt{2} = \sqrt{242}A$.

Hence, the value of~$x = 242$.

questions.q: The effective current $I$ in the given circuit at very high frequencies will be _____~$A$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
At very high frequencies,& inductor acts as an open circuit& and capacitor as short circuit.

So, capacitive reactance,& ${X}_{C} = \dfrac{1}{ωC} ≈ 0$

Also, inductive reactance,~${X}_{L} = ωL ≈ \infty$

Thus, equivalent circuit can be redrawn as

Here, both~$4Ω$~resistances are in parallel and together they are in series with$1Ω$~and~$2Ω$~resistances.

Equivalent impedance is~$Z = 1 + \dfrac{4 × 4}{4 + 4} + 2 = 5Ω$

Effective current is~$I = \dfrac{220V}{5Ω} = 44A$
